items.title: Equipment Material Consumption Entry
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Meter Readings, Utilisation and Production › Equipment Material Consumption Entry

cards.title: Why consumption of issued material is recorded per equipment
cards.body:
This consumption entry records how much of each item issued from stores was actually consumed on a piece of equipment, and in which of its components.
Maintenance staff use it after items issued to equipment or a maintenance order have been used.
Issued stock is matched with consumed quantity per equipment and per component.

cards.title: Eligible issue lines and splitting consumption by component
cards.body:
Only lines from authorised issues of the same company and division are offered, for items that the equipment's parts list marks as needing a consumption entry.
The issue must have been made for a maintenance order or to the equipment's own cost center.
At least one line must be selected, and for each line the quantities entered against components must add up exactly to the line quantity.
A balance of issued less consumed and returned quantity is shown for guidance but not enforced.

items.title: Production Entry
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Meter Readings, Utilisation and Production › Production Entry

cards.title: What the simplified Production Entry records
cards.body:
Production Entry records the output of one shift at one work center, with item, quantity and value per output line.
Production or plant supervisors enter it at the end of a shift or run when finished or semi-finished goods are declared.
Output reaches stock only through an authorised document, and each line carries a value for costing.

cards.title: Output lines, rates and receipt into stock
cards.body:
Output lines offer finished and semi-finished item types according to the line type.
Each line needs an item and a non-zero quantity, and loss quantity cannot exceed it.
The receipt rate is value divided by quantity, and it is set to zero unless the company's finance settings allow it.
When authorised, each output line is received into the warehouse, and the issued lot balance is checked against the lots recorded on the entry.

items.title: Axle and Wheel Configuration
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Tyre Management › Axle and Wheel Configuration

cards.title: What an Axle and Wheel Configuration defines
cards.body:
Axle and Wheel Configuration defines a reusable vehicle layout: how many axles and tyres a vehicle type has and where each tyre sits.
Fleet maintenance staff create it before vehicles or tyres are assigned to a new configuration, such as a two-axle truck or a trailer with spares.
Tyres can then be fitted, moved and inspected against named positions.

cards.title: Positions, axles and matching totals
cards.body:
At least one tyre position must be defined.
A running position needs a non-zero axle number, while other positions, such as spares, have no axle.
The number of positions must equal the number of tyres, and the number of distinct axles must equal the number of axles stated.
Vehicles reference the layout, and tyre fitment only offers positions that exist on it, so a wrong layout blocks correct tyre tracking.

items.title: Tyre Category Master
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Tyre Management › Tyre Category Master

cards.title: What a Tyre Category defines
cards.body:
The Tyre Category Master defines the classes into which tyres are grouped, such as by construction or application, with default tread depth standards.
The maintenance team maintains it when a new class of tyre is introduced or standards change.
Tread depth standards are held once per category and make instead of being retyped on every tyre.

cards.title: Category codes, tread depth values and make-specific standards
cards.body:
A new category receives an automatic code and is authorised on save.
Each category carries an original and a threshold tread depth, entered with one decimal place.
Make-specific values can be added for tyre makes of the company, and lines without a make are ignored.
When a tyre is registered, its tread depths default from the category's make line if one exists, otherwise from the category defaults.

items.title: Tyre Repair Category
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Tyre Management › Tyre Repair Category

cards.title: What a Tyre Repair Category classifies
cards.body:
The Tyre Repair Category defines the kinds of repair work that can be done on a tyre, each tied to a repair type, an optional service item and permitted roles.
The maintenance team maintains it when a new kind of repair is introduced or responsibilities change.
Repairs are classified uniformly and linked to the service bought or performed.

cards.title: Codes, roles, service items and the retread type
cards.body:
A new category receives an automatic code and is authorised on save.
At least one permitted role must be selected.
The service item is optional and can be left empty when the repair is not bought as a service.
The repair type matters downstream: a retread category limits repair requests to tyres awaiting retread, while other categories apply to installed tyres or tyres awaiting repair.

items.title: Tyre Master
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Tyre Management › Tyre Master

cards.title: What the Tyre Master register holds
cards.body:
The Tyre Master registers every individual tyre the company owns, whether in stock, fitted to a vehicle or at another stage of its life.
Fleet maintenance staff create it when a tyre is purchased, received from a material issue or brought in as opening stock.
Each tyre can be followed through fitment, removal, repair and retreading.

cards.title: Tyre identity, source and current location
cards.body:
A tyre can be registered directly or from a material issue of a serialised tyre item, which fills serial number, make and description.
An installed tyre needs a vehicle, a free position on its layout, an install date and tread depth; any other status needs a warehouse.
Purchase order, invoice and opening tread depth each need their dates.
Tread depths default from the category, and the threshold must be lower than the original depth.

items.title: Tyre Movement
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Tyre Management › Tyre Movement

cards.title: What a Tyre Movement records
cards.body:
Tyre Movement records tyres being fitted to, removed from, replaced on or swapped between wheel positions, with readings at that moment.
Workshop staff record it whenever tyres are changed on a vehicle.
The current position and life history of every tyre stays correct, and tyre life can be measured.

cards.title: Install, remove, replace and swap rules
cards.body:
Every line needs a vehicle, a position, an action and an assignee, and the fitment or removal date is mandatory.
Installing uses a free position and a tyre that is in stock, removed, repaired or retreaded, with its tread depth and readings.
Removing or replacing needs a fitted tyre, its readings and a reason, plus a new status and warehouse except for swaps.
Swaps need a different position, or a different vehicle for a cross-vehicle swap.

cards.title: How authorised tyre movements update tyre history
cards.body:
Nothing changes on the tyres until the movement is authorised.
On authorisation each line updates the tyre's status, life stage, vehicle and position, and adds a history entry with the readings taken.
The update refuses to install a tyre that is already installed, to remove one that is not installed, to replace with a tyre that is not available, or to swap tyres that are not fitted.
A removed tyre goes to waiting after removal, awaiting repair or awaiting retread, which feeds the repair and status change process.
Because readings are captured at fitment and removal, distance and hours per tyre can be calculated for each life stage.

items.title: Tyre Inspection Entry
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Tyre Management › Tyre Inspection Entry

cards.title: Why tyre tread depth is inspected and recorded
cards.body:
Tyre Inspection Entry records dated tread depth readings and tyre condition for a set of tyres, with the inspector and shift.
Workshop or fleet inspectors record it during routine tyre checks.
A history of tread wear per tyre supports life analysis and replacement decisions.

cards.title: Inspection lines and average tread depth
cards.body:
Lines can be entered by vehicle and position, which fills the tyre fitted there today, or by choosing the tyre directly.
At least one line is required, each with a tyre and a tread depth; vehicle-wise lines also need vehicle and position.
Up to five tread depth readings can be taken, and the first is mandatory.
The line's tread depth is the average of the non-zero readings, shown to one decimal place.

items.title: Tyre Repair Request
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Tyre Management › Tyre Repair Request

cards.title: Why tyre repairs are requested formally
cards.body:
A Tyre Repair Request records which tyres are sent for repair or retread, where, and why.
Workshop or fleet staff raise it when installed or removed tyres need repair, or tyres awaiting retread are sent out.
Repair work is requested through an authorised document, and retread hand-over is traceable in tyre history.

cards.title: Repair category, eligible tyres and retread hand-over
cards.body:
The repair category decides which tyres are listed: retread categories list only tyres awaiting retread, others list installed tyres or those awaiting repair; changing it reloads the list.
Lines are entered by vehicle and position, or by choosing a tyre that is not installed, and retreads allow only the latter.
Every line needs a tyre and a repair description, with optional current tread depth.
On authorisation of a retread request, each tyre moves to under retread with a history entry.

items.title: Tyre Repair Entry
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Tyre Management › Tyre Repair Entry

cards.title: What a Tyre Repair Entry records
cards.body:
Tyre Repair Entry records the outcome of repair and retread work per tyre: the status reached, tread depth and distance, cost, assignee and, for retreads, the new tread depth and expected life.
Workshop staff record it when tyres come back from repair or retread, or are rejected.
Tyre condition, life stage, cost and next status are updated through one controlled document.

cards.title: Eligible tyres, allowed results and line rules
cards.body:
Entries can be direct or against a repair request; retread categories list tyres awaiting or under retread, and other categories list installed tyres or those awaiting repair.
Repairs can end as repair completed or rejected, and retreads as retread completed or retread rejected.
Every line needs a tyre, a repair status, an assignee and remarks, and a completed retread needs a new tread depth above the threshold.
For requests, only selected lines are saved, and the request becomes completed or in progress accordingly.

cards.title: Proof for external work and moving tyres to the next life stage
cards.body:
When the request sent tyres to an external repairer, a supplier and location are required.
A tyre completed externally needs a service receipt note against the request, and a rejected tyre needs an authorised gate pass in, so the physical return is proven.
On authorisation, the tyre takes its repair status when the category is a retread or the tyre was awaiting repair.
A completed retread moves the tyre to its next life stage with the new tread depth, so wear and cost are tracked separately for each life.
This links workshop results, vendor documents and tyre history in one step.

items.title: Change Tyre Status
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Tyre Management › Change Tyre Status

cards.title: Why removed tyres get a formal status change
cards.body:
Change Tyre Status moves removed tyres to their next decision: awaiting repair, awaiting retread or scrapped, and closes the case of a rejected retread.
Fleet maintenance staff use it when a removed tyre is judged.
Status changes are authorised, reasoned and traceable instead of edited on the tyre record.

cards.title: Allowed tyre status moves and what authorisation does
cards.body:
Only tyres waiting after removal, awaiting repair, awaiting retread or with a rejected retread are offered.
The new status is limited by the current one, and a tyre can never be set to installed here.
Every tyre line needs a reason and a new status, and earlier reasons can be reused.
Only when the document is authorised does each tyre's status change and enter the tyre history; scrapping closes the tyre's current life stage.

items.title: Tyre Expense Entry
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Tyre Management › Tyre Expense Entry

cards.title: Why tyre expenses are booked separately
cards.body:
Tyre Expense Entry books costs incurred on individual tyres, such as fitting or balancing charges, that are not part of a purchase or a repair document.
Fleet or workshop staff record it whenever such a cost is incurred.
Total cost of ownership per tyre and per life stage can be measured.

cards.title: Vehicle-wise and tyre-wise expense lines
cards.body:
Lines can be entered by vehicle and position, which fills the fitted tyre, or by choosing the tyre directly.
Every line needs a tyre and a non-zero amount, and vehicle-wise lines also need a vehicle and position.
Tyres that are not scrapped are offered, and the tyre's current status and life stage are copied onto the line.
The total is the sum of the lines, and each status change stamps the user and time.

items.title: Incident Entry
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Incidents and Insurance Claims › Incident Entry

cards.title: Why incidents involving equipment are recorded
cards.body:
Incident Entry records an accident, breakdown or damage involving a vehicle or equipment, with the people involved, damaged parts and the reviews required.
Fleet or safety staff enter it when an incident is reported.
Each incident is captured once with all facts, so management can review it and decide on insurance.

cards.title: People, damaged parts and status of an incident
cards.body:
Every employee involved needs an incident narration and the person the incident was reported to.
Damaged parts are recorded by name, and an existing part only has its description updated.
Checks run in order, from document details through general details and employees to reviews, and the first failure stops the save.
Release and authorisation stamp the user and time, and only authorised incidents move on to review.

items.title: Incident Review
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Incidents and Insurance Claims › Incident Review

cards.title: Purpose of an Incident Review
cards.body:
An Incident Review records one function's assessment of an authorised incident, such as operations, fleet, technical, human resources or management.
Each reviewer records it when their review falls due in the incident's sequence.
Every incident is assessed by all required functions, ending in a management decision and a decision on insurance.

cards.title: Review sequence, editable details and insurance decision
cards.body:
Only authorised incidents that require the chosen review type are offered, and each type can review an incident only once.
The first review in the sequence is always allowed, and a later one only after the preceding review is recorded.
Each review type edits its own details: operations, fleet and human resources record cause and action, technical adds damage and expenses, and management records only the final decision.
Only the technical review can flag an insurance claim, and a deduction amount needs a narration.

cards.title: How review results are written back to the incident
cards.body:
A review does not just sit beside the incident; each save writes its damage amount, deduction amount, deduction narration, responsible employee and insurance flag back onto the incident itself.
Damage and deduction amounts are stored only when they are above zero.
Remarks can be recorded per damaged part, and only parts with a remark are kept.
Because the insurance flag can only be set in the technical review, an insurance claim can only follow a technical assessment.
The incident therefore always shows the latest agreed financial impact, which drives employee deductions and any insurance claim that is raised against it afterwards.

items.title: Insurance Claim
items.context: Plant Maintenance › Incidents and Insurance Claims › Insurance Claim

cards.title: What an Insurance Claim records
cards.body:
An Insurance Claim ties one incident, one insured vehicle or equipment and one insurance policy document to a claim amount and a company liability amount.
Fleet or insurance staff raise it after an incident is marked as needing a claim and a policy document exists.
Each such incident is claimed once, against a known policy, with the split between insurer and company recorded.

cards.title: Claim date, policy validity and previous claims
cards.body:
The claim date cannot be earlier than the date the incident was reported.
The policy is shown as valid when its validity date is on or after the claim date and as expired otherwise; this is informational and does not stop the claim.
The latest earlier claim against the same equipment and policy is shown for reference, helping avoid duplicate claims.
Release and authorisation stamp the user and time.
